newsitem.title: GERMANY: BA Germany cargo hit by poor Heathrow standards.
newsitem.headline: BA Germany cargo hit by poor Heathrow standards.

text.p: Poor quality standards at Heathrow have hit British Airways World Cargo sales in Germany, Mark Gardiner, the airline's cargo manager Central Europe, said.
The German air cargo industry lost confidence in BAWC last year and the airline's market share suffered, he said in a Reuters interview.
"We are below our targeted tonnage by six percent (and) we are down on our budgeted yield by 10 percent," Gardiner said.
"We have paid the price for inconsistent service levels (at Heathrow) and we have to work hard to get market confidence back."
But improved cargo handling standards at Heathrow and the internal business re-engineering would pay off in the long- term, he added.
BA flies most of its ex-Germany cargo from Frankfurt or Dusseldorf to Heathrow or Gatwick for onward intercontinental transportation.

As a short-term measure, spot rate offers for cargo up to 48 hours before departure allowed BA to improve its North Atlantic market share by more than one percent last autumn, Gardiner said. Spot rates would be offered for some African, Middle East, Far East and Caribbean destinations over the coming months, he added.
BA was also planning to target customers in Germany more actively this year with specific offers.
